title: The Mystery of the Disappearing Puddle
content: Have you ever noticed that a puddle on the street completely disappears after a sunny day? It doesn't sink into the concrete. So, where does the water go?

title: Pause and Think
content: Why do you think the water vanishes? If it goes up into the air, why can't we see it? What would happen if we put a lid over the puddle?

content.title: Water Molecules Escaping
content.description: Watch how the heat from the sun gives energy to the liquid water, allowing it to turn into an invisible gas and rise up.

title: Evaporation
content: The water hasn't vanished! Heat from the sun turns the liquid water into a gas called water vapor. This process is called Evaporation. (Etymology: from Latin 'evaporare', meaning to disperse in vapor).

question: What happens to a puddle of water on a hot sunny day?
options: It gets absorbed by the sun.
It turns into water vapor through evaporation.
It sinks completely into solid rocks.

title: Reflect on this
content: Imagine you are trying to dry your wet clothes faster. Using what you know about evaporation, what would you do? Explain it in your own words.

title: Connecting the Dots
content: Evaporation doesn't just happen to puddles. It happens to oceans, rivers, and even the sweat on your skin! This rising water vapor eventually cools down to form clouds.

title: Mini Challenge
content: Take two identical bowls with the same amount of water. Keep one in direct sunlight and the other in a dark cupboard. After 2 days, check which bowl has less water. You have just measured evaporation!

title: The Sweaty Glass Mystery
content: Take a glass of ice-cold water out of the fridge and leave it on a table. After a few minutes, you'll see water droplets forming on the OUTSIDE of the glass. The glass isn't leaking! So, where did this water come from?

title: Pause and Think
content: If the water didn't come from inside the glass, what is the only other place it could have come from? What happens to the invisible water vapor in the air when it touches the cold glass?

content.title: Invisible Vapor to Visible Drops
content.description: The warm air around the glass contains invisible water vapor. When it touches the cold glass, it cools down and turns back into liquid water drops.

title: Condensation
content: When water vapor cools down, it turns back into liquid water. This process is called Condensation. (Etymology: from Latin 'condensare', meaning to make dense). This is exactly how clouds are formed high up in the cold sky!

question: Which of the following is an example of condensation?
options: Drying wet clothes in the sun.
Water droplets forming on a cold glass.

title: Reflect on this
content: Have you ever breathed out on a cold winter morning and seen your breath look like smoke? Try to explain what is happening using the word 'condensation'.

title: Connecting the Dots
content: Condensation is the opposite of evaporation. Together, they create the Water Cycle. When the condensed drops in clouds get too heavy, they fall back down to Earth as precipitation.

title: Cloud in a Jar
content: Pour some warm water into a glass jar. Light a match, quickly blow it out, and drop it in the jar. Put a bag of ice on top. Watch as a mini-cloud forms inside! You have recreated condensation.

title: Teacher's Secret
content: In ancient Indian texts, the process of the water cycle was beautifully described. The Aditya Hridayam and various Puranas mention how the sun's rays 'drink' water from the oceans and return it as life-giving rain.

title: Watch Out!
content: Many students think that boiling is the same as evaporation. Remember: Evaporation happens at ANY temperature, even room temperature. Boiling only happens when water is heated to 100°C.
